doc.title: Virginia Mayhew interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, May 23, 2022

title: Navigating unusual chords and seeking challenge
summary: Without perfect pitch she works chord by chord; Billy Mintz tells her to just play. She likes deep-end challenges, perhaps from karate.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: What to think while improvising: wrong notes and being in the moment

blocks.x: Nor do I. And when I am playing with a pianist especially who uses what — I will use your term also, sort of weird chords, do you have a way of finding your way in them?

Well it depends if I have a chance to work on the stuff, which I did with Roberta’s music. So I would sit at the piano and I would play those chords and I would see what do I hear over that. And I had to do it chord by chord because there are so many of them. But I’m starting to hear them now and if I don’t have that, like recently I did a rehearsal with Billy Mintz — do you know him? A great drummer? And he has this tune, it’s really hard. Anyhow, it’s just really hard tune — and he said, “Don’t look at the chord changes, don’t think about the chord changes, just play.” And if I don’t know what’s going on with the harmony on that kind of stuff I just play, you know, and try to make melodies and create something. Because you can’t, unless they’re playing one of those chords for a long time you can’t really catch it. I mean what’s your experience with that?
Well I find that I probably avoid the situations.

I like to put myself in challenging situations. I think that might come from my karate training. Maybe not, I don’t know. Maybe not. But I like to be challenged. Not that I’m not challenged by anything, but I like to really throw myself into the deep end. And fortunately I have friends and peers that like to do that.
